shows.show: Earn Your Leisure (Troy Millings & Rashad Bilal)

who_books.claim: Co-founded in 2018 by Rashad Bilal and Troy Millings; operates as a podcast plus media network (EYL Network) and online learning community.
Personality and story are the deciding factors for Bilal 'and his team' when choosing guests. No individual booking producer is publicly named in sources found.
A search snippet says the EYL Instagram points bookings and inquiries to @valid_asow. Not confirmed on the profile itself, so verify before using.
Hosts' speaking (stage) bookings go through The Shark Group speakers bureau. That is a different route from podcast guest booking.

Invest Fest is the pipeline: speakers and sponsors flow into the podcast universe. Sponsorship is booked through investfest.com (Partner With Us / Partnership Packages, 'book a meeting with the team'); exhibitors use the vendor app and vendor@investfest.com.
Being on stage or sponsoring at Invest Fest is the warmest way into an EYL episode, since the hosts record content around the festival.

route.claim: No public 'be a guest' form or guest email was found. Directory listings (Rephonic, Muck Rack) advertise contacts behind paywalls.

Invest Fest sponsorship: 'visit the Sponsors page and book a meeting with the team'. Packages cover on-site activations, off-site events, media placements and digital integrations. 2025 on-site sponsorships sold out.

Invest Fest vendor route: 'complete the vendor form... after submitting the form, place an order for your vendor booth'. 'Beverage, Food and Smoking Products are NOT Permitted.' Questions go to vendor@investfest.com.
No public open-call speaker application for Invest Fest was found. The speaker lineup appears to be curated or invite-only.
Best route: an agent-to-team intro (David Harris to the EYL team via the Instagram booking contact or an Invest Fest partnerships meeting), not a cold form.

criteria.claim: 'Personality and story are the decisive factors.' The aim is to let celebrities and entrepreneurs share their lives in ways people don't usually see, as a vehicle for financial education.
They invite Black entertainers, artists, business owners, investors and millionaires to talk about their path to success. A turning point was interviewing ex-Bad Boy executive Derek Ferguson in 2019.
They want listeners to take lessons they can apply. Guests need actionable takeaways, not just a life story.
Critics, including on Reddit, have accused EYL of 'unvetted guests'. Expect the team to care about credibility and disclosure.

logistics.claim: Atlanta has been the company's home for six years and hosts the annual Invest Fest. The company is also listed as New York-based.
Corporate listings place EYL in New York (White Plains / NYC).
Formats include long-form interviews, 'Study Hall' educational episodes (e.g. Wall Street Trapper) and topical tutorials.
No specific studio address, episode length or lead time was found. Plan on in-person recording in Atlanta or NYC, booked weeks ahead.

what_works.claim: Art as an asset class has been covered before: 'Art Investing for Beginners' with collector Ingrid Best (40-50 pieces), and EYL #129 with Troy Carter (manager of Lady Gaga and John Legend, art collector) on art and angel investing.
EYL #129 'Music Streaming, Art Investing, Angel Investing' with Troy Carter.
Pitch numbers and education (how an artist's market is built, how prices and editions work, how to buy blue-chip art) rather than celebrity gossip.

what_fails.claim: Pitches that look like a paid promo or an unvetted 'guru' will probably fail, given public backlash over vetting and paywalled content.
Rashad Bilal addressed Invest Fest backlash in August 2026 and stressed it is 'not a Black conference'. Avoid framing that leans on that controversy.

hooks_timing.claim: Invest Fest 2026 took place August 7-9, 2026 (some listings say Aug 21-22) at the Georgia World Congress Center, Atlanta, with 40,000+ attendees expected.
Invest Fest 2027 returns to Atlanta in August 2027. Exact dates TBA.
Invest Fest also runs a Bahamas edition, a possible second stage.
Timing: pitch a podcast taping now (Q4 2026) and pitch Invest Fest 2027 programming or an 'art as an asset' activation in Q1 2027, before sponsorships sell out as they did in 2025.

avery.angle: Art as an alternative asset for the culture: how Avery built Alec Monopoly from street graffiti into a global luxury brand, how ArtLife opened up blue-chip buying online, and how he bought early into Black artists (Hebru Brantley, Jammie Holmes) whose markets then took off. Frame it as a tutorial (how to buy your first real artwork, avoid fakes, read editions) plus the business story behind it.
avery.subject_line: Guest pitch: The dealer who turned Alec Monopoly into a global brand on art as an asset for the culture
avery.proof: artnet profile '9 Questions for Avery Andon, Alec Monopoly's Dealer and Manager' (https://news.artnet.com/partner-content/dealer-avery-andon-alec-monopoly); Coveteur on ArtLife as 'luxury investments for all' (https://coveteur.com/artlife-art-gallery); ArtLife's Alec Monopoly investment guide (https://artlife.com/news/alec-monopoly-investment-guide/); his own ArtLife with Avery Andon podcast (https://creators.spotify.com/pod/profile/artlife-podcast/).
avery.notes: Past art guests are collectors Ingrid Best and Troy Carter. No dealer guest and no Monopoly, Brantley or Holmes link to EYL was found. That gap is the pitch: EYL has done art for beginners but never had a working dealer explain how artist markets are built. Pair the pitch with an Invest Fest 2027 'Art as an Asset' panel.

who_books.claim: IMDb Pro lists the producers as Randy Acker, Kareem 'Biggs' Burke and Lee Sanchez.
Kareem 'Biggs' Burke (Roc-A-Fella co-founder) is a producer on Drink Champs and an executive who manages N.O.R.E.

Since Sept 2025 the show sits in 'The Drink Champs Podcast Network', a partnership with iHeartMedia and Charlamagne Tha God's The Black Effect Podcast Network. Before that it was with WMG's Interval Presents (2023), which shut down.
Black Effect backs the new Drink Champs network. Earlier deals included Tidal, Revolt and Mass Appeal.
DJ EFN's LinkedIn lists him under 'Drink Champs LLC'. He is Miami-based and runs Crazy Hood Productions.
Booking is relationship-driven through the hosts and Biggs's circle. Agents should go through iHeart/Black Effect partnerships or a direct personal connection to N.O.R.E. or EFN.

route.claim: A search snippet cited a contact email listed in podcast directories (drinkchamps@gmail.com). It is not confirmed on an official Drink Champs page and may be stale. Verify before use.
drinkchamps.com has an About page. No guest submission form was found.
Fan-submission calls have run (e.g. 10-year anniversary shoutouts) but are not guest routes.

criteria.claim: DJ EFN: 'the idea is to talk to guests from our generation. We want those with at least ten-year careers that aren't on a press run. It's about fluid conversation and drinking.'
EFN: 'Guests don't have to drink, but the alcohol is a star of the show... like watching your uncles getting belligerent, and in between, you get all these nuggets of history.'
The network launch is described as bringing 'new voices' and storytelling 'rooted in hip-hop and beyond', which opens room for culture-adjacent non-rappers.

logistics.claim: Drink Champs (X): 'We film in a working bar in the heart of Miami's art district. It's live and direct! Our slogan is the most professional unprofessional podcast!'
Recorded at the hosts' Wynwood studio. Past locations include EFN's South Miami studio, a South Beach hotel lobby and Little Haiti.
Live and road tapings happen, e.g. a D'USSE mobile studio at Rolling Loud Miami (2023) and Revolt Music Conference episodes.
Episodes are long (often 2+ hours) and unscripted, with alcohol on set. Prep consists of having stories ready, not talking points.

what_works.claim: Non-rapper executives have been booked when they carry hip-hop history: Lyor Cohen and Kevin Liles (Ep. 41, at Revolt Music Conference), Steve Stoute with Tone of Trackmasters (Ep. 105), and Kareem 'Biggs' Burke (Ep. 113, 166).
Non-music celebrities such as Mike Tyson have appeared.

Art Week tie-in exists: Drink Champs held a live recording at Arlo Wynwood / the Art of Hip Hop Museum during Art Basel, and N.O.R.E. and EFN appeared at the Museum of Graffiti on Dec 5, 2024 (with a Steve Stoute keynote).
Pairing a non-rapper with a legend they are tied to (as with Steve Stoute + Tone) is the proven format. Avery is best booked alongside a hip-hop figure he advises or a Miami street-art legend.

what_fails.claim: Guests 'on a press run' and short-career guests are explicitly not what they want.
Stiff, media-trained or sales-led guests clash with the 'most professional unprofessional' bar format.

hooks_timing.claim: Art Basel Miami Beach 2026 runs Dec 4-6 (VIP Dec 2-3) at the Miami Beach Convention Center. Miami Art Week is the natural window, and Drink Champs has done Art Week live tapings in Wynwood.
10-year anniversary was June 11, 2026, with 17.6B watch minutes. N.O.R.E. is pushing radio and multimedia formats.
New iHeart/Black Effect network (Sept 2025) is seeking new shows and voices. A side-pitch is possible: an art and culture spin-off segment.
Pitch by early November 2026 for an Art Week (Dec 2-6) Wynwood taping.

avery.angle: Miami's art-world plug for hip-hop: the Miami dealer who turned a graffiti kid (Alec Monopoly) into a global luxury brand and quietly advises rappers on what to buy. Pitch an Art Week Wynwood episode, ideally with a hip-hop client or collector beside him, full of stories about celebrities buying art and street art going blue-chip.
avery.subject_line: Art Week Drink Champs: the Miami dealer behind Alec Monopoly and hip-hop's art collections
avery.proof: artnet '9 Questions for Avery Andon, Alec Monopoly's Dealer and Manager' (https://news.artnet.com/partner-content/dealer-avery-andon-alec-monopoly); Alec Monopoly Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alec_Monopoly); ArtLife with Avery Andon podcast featuring artists, actors and musicians (https://creators.spotify.com/pod/profile/artlife-podcast/).
avery.notes: No past Drink Champs guest linked to Alec Monopoly, Hebru Brantley or Jammie Holmes was found, and no dealer guest was found. EFN's '10-year career, not on a press run' rule suits Avery's long record, but the show favours hip-hop storytellers. Lead with the celebrity-client stories (names only with consent) and the Miami/Wynwood tie. Go through Biggs Burke or Black Effect partnerships rather than the unverified gmail.

who_books.claim: Hosted by actor and collector Russell Tovey and gallerist Robert Diament, who met at a Tracey Emin retrospective. Guests come from their own art-world circle.
Produced by Spiritland Productions (with them since the first episode) and OffScript. Premiered Oct 19, 2018.
Published enquiries contact: talkart@independenttalent.com, via Independent Talent (Tovey's agency), listed in the show's feed and directory entry.
Russell Tovey is represented by Independent Talent.
Dealers and gallerists DO appear: Sadie Coles (Mar 21, 2019) and Maureen Paley (S14E5, Oct 6, 2022). Matthew Slotover (Frieze co-founder) was the Season 27 finale.

route.claim: Email talkart@independenttalent.com, the only published route found. No 'suggest a guest' form was found. Instagram: instagram.com/talkart.
Show tagline: 'exclusive interviews with leading artists, curators & gallerists, and even occasionally their talented friends from other industries like acting, music and journalism'.

criteria.claim: Guests are mostly contemporary artists, curators, gallerists and collectors, plus famous art-loving friends (Elton John, Stephen Fry, Paul Smith, Radiohead, Lena Dunham).
The hosts 'venerate artists and enjoy supporting emerging talent'. Mission: make art accessible, push back on elitism, 'geek out'.
Wish list of superstar artists: David Hockney, Marlene Dumas, Nicole Eisenman.
Episodes are often pegged to a current show (e.g. S28 opener John Currin at his Sadie Coles show; Lewis Hammond at The Hepworth Wakefield).

logistics.claim: Episodes run about an hour (e.g. Jammie Holmes: 1h11m).
Recorded mostly in London and UK venues (e.g. live at Maison Estelle; Nevill Holt Festival 2025 with Harland Miller), sometimes in artists' studios abroad (Jammie Holmes in his Dallas studio).
Recorded in Miami during Basel week, Dec 2025, with HUGO BOSS creative director Marco Falcioni on the Art Basel Awards.
Runs in seasons (S27 from Feb 2026, S28 in 2026). Some 2026 episodes are hosted by Diament solo.
Diament's gallery has moved to Margate, Kent.

what_works.claim: Artists with a show on, or a story about collecting, are the core booking. Brand/fair partnerships (HUGO BOSS x Art Basel Awards) are booked around art-fair weeks.
Jammie Holmes was a guest (S15E6, Dec 16, 2022), recorded at his Dallas studio. This is a direct link to an artist Avery championed early.
Pitch Avery as a collector-dealer with stories, not a salesman. Ideally offer a joint episode with an artist he champions or a Miami Art Week recording.

what_fails.claim: Market or price-led talk ('art as investment') runs against the show's anti-elitist, artist-first ethos. Commercial street-art branding may be a hard sell to UK art-world hosts.
No episode found with Alec Monopoly or Hebru Brantley.

hooks_timing.claim: Frieze London 2026: Oct 14-18, The Regent's Park (Oct 14 invitation only). It is a regular topic for the hosts, but too close to pitch for now. Target Frieze 2027.
Art Basel Miami Beach 2026: Dec 4-6 (VIP Dec 2-3). Talk Art recorded in Miami during Basel week in 2025, so a 2026 repeat is the best window.
Pitch by late Oct 2026 for a Miami Art Week recording slot (e.g. offer a venue or studio visit with a Miami artist).

avery.angle: The Miami collector-dealer who backed Jammie Holmes, a past Talk Art guest, and Hebru Brantley early. Offer a Miami Art Week conversation about spotting artists before the institutions do, opening art to new collectors (ArtLife online, hip-hop and celebrity clients) and the street-to-gallery path. Lead with artists, not prices.
avery.subject_line: Miami Art Week idea for Talk Art: Avery Andon, early champion of Jammie Holmes and Hebru Brantley
avery.proof: Talk Art's Jammie Holmes episode (https://podcasts.apple.com/ie/podcast/jammie-holmes/id1439567112?i=1000590338640); artnet '9 Questions for Avery Andon' (https://news.artnet.com/partner-content/dealer-avery-andon-alec-monopoly); Coveteur on ArtLife (https://coveteur.com/artlife-art-gallery).
avery.notes: Send to talkart@independenttalent.com (published). Dealer precedent: Sadie Coles, Maureen Paley, Matthew Slotover. Diament is a gallerist himself, so dealer talk is native. Avoid the Alec Monopoly / investment framing as the headline and mention it as a credential only. Treat Avery's role with Holmes and Brantley as client-supplied claims; the sources found here do not document it.

general_tips.claim: Most podcast hosts find guests through their own network, past collaborators and referrals, and only sometimes through cold outreach. Warm intros beat forms on all three shows.
Tie each pitch to a live moment: Art Basel Miami Beach (Dec 2-6, 2026) works for Drink Champs (Wynwood) and Talk Art (2025 precedent); Invest Fest (Aug 2027, Atlanta) for EYL.
Avery already hosts the 'ArtLife with Avery Andon' podcast with artists, actors and musicians. Offering a reciprocal episode is a useful sweetener.
Avery is listed as an expert source on Qwoted, which can serve as a press-credibility link.
Search budget: 37/37 used. Gaps: no named guest-booking producer for EYL or Talk Art; Drink Champs gmail and EYL @valid_asow are unverified snippets.
